transcript.text: Our Henry has gone a bit weak and sounds rough, sort of rattly growl instead of the normal hum. It's about 12 years old. Bags and filter are new. Worth fixing?

Usually yes. Henrys are built to be repaired, parts are cheap and easy to find, and a new one costs roughly £150-200. Unless the body is cracked or the cable is badly damaged, it's almost always worth fixing.

### Rule out the easy stuff first (unplugged)
1. Hose and tools blocked. Drop a coin through the hose or shine a torch down it. Check the wand and floor tool too. A blockage alone causes weak suction and a strained, higher-pitched note.
2. Hose split or cracked, especially near the cuff ends. Air leaks kill suction.
3. Seal between the head and tub. Make sure the head sits squarely and the clips are tight.
4. The cloth filter. You've replaced it, but check it's seated properly with no gaps.

If all of that's fine, the noise points to the motor.

### The likely culprit: the motor
A rattly growl instead of a hum at 12 years old is the classic sign of:
• Worn motor bearings. This is the most likely cause given the sound. They get rough and noisy, and the motor slows down, so suction drops.
• Debris in the fan, for example if something got past a split bag or filter at some point and chipped the impeller.
• Worn carbon brushes. These cause weak or intermittent running and sometimes sparking or a burning smell, but they're less likely to cause a rattle.

### Fixing it
• Replacement motor: usually about £30-60 online. Search for your model (e.g. HVR200) plus "motor". Numatic and plenty of spares sites stock them.
• Fitting: it's a straightforward DIY job for most people. Undo the screws on the head, unclip a couple of connectors, and swap the motor over. There are good YouTube videos for each model.
• If you'd rather not DIY, a local vacuum repair shop will typically do it for a modest labour charge.
• Brushes alone are only a few pounds, but with the rattle you're probably better off replacing the whole motor so you get new bearings and brushes in one go.

### When it's not worth it
• There's a burning smell or visible damage beyond the motor, like a melted housing or damaged wiring.
• The cable or switch is also failing and the total parts cost is creeping towards the price of a new one.

Bottom line: check for blockages and leaks, and if those are fine, fit a new motor. For about £40 and half an hour, you'll likely get another decade out of it.
Thank you. You mention a burning smell, and now that you say it, there is a hot, electrical sort of smell after it has been running for about five minutes. Does that change things?

Yes, it changes things a bit, mainly around safety. It doesn't necessarily mean the Henry is beyond saving.

### First: stop using it for now
A hot electrical smell means something is overheating. A motor with failing bearings has to work harder, gets hot, and can eventually burn out its windings or, in rare cases, become a fire risk. Unplug it and don't run it again until it's sorted.

### What's likely going on
With the rattle, weak suction and a smell that builds after a few minutes, the most likely story is:
• Worn bearings dragging, making the motor labour and overheat
• Worn carbon brushes arcing, which gives a sharp, electrical, slightly "ozone" smell
• Windings starting to overheat or break down, the more serious end of the same problem

All three point to the motor, which is the part you'd be replacing anyway.

### Quick checks (unplugged)
1. Plug and cable: look for scorch marks, discoloration, melted or soft spots, or a plug that gets hot. Check the full length of the cable, especially where it enters the head and near the plug.
2. Switch area: any browning or melting around the on/off switch.
3. Inside the head (if you're comfortable removing the screws): look for blackened or melted plastic, scorched wires, or a burnt-looking motor.

### Is it still worth fixing?
• If the damage is confined to the motor: yes. A new motor fixes the noise, the suction and the smell, since you're replacing the part that's overheating.
• If you find melted housing, scorched wiring or a damaged switch beyond the motor: it may still be fixable, because switches and cables are also cheap. But if it's widespread, or you're not confident judging it, have a repair shop look at it or consider replacing the vacuum.

If you do the motor swap yourself, make sure all connections are tight and correctly fitted. Loose connections are another source of heat. Afterwards, run it while you're nearby for the first few sessions to confirm the smell has gone. If you'd rather not deal with the electrical side, this is a good case for letting a vacuum repair shop do it.

Thank you, I've unplugged it. The plug and cable look fine and aren't damaged, and the plug isn't hot. I should also say that when I looked at the grille on top in the dim hall, I saw blue-orange sparks flickering inside. I'm not confident taking the motor out myself. Is it safe to carry on using it?

## No, don't use it again until it's repaired

Those sparks settle it. Carbon-brush motors like the Henry's always make a tiny bit of sparking where the brushes touch the spinning part of the motor (the commutator). You wouldn't normally see it through the grille. Visible blue-orange flickering, together with the hot electrical smell and the rattle, means heavy arcing. The brushes are worn down and/or the commutator is damaged. That arcing is what's causing the smell. It generates a lot of heat, can burn out the motor, and in the worst case could ignite dust inside the machine.

So keep it unplugged and put it aside until it's been sorted.

### The good news
Your plug and cable are fine, so the problem looks confined to the motor. That's the best-case version of this fault, and it's very fixable.

### Getting it repaired without DIY
• Local vacuum repair shop: Search "vacuum repair near me". Henrys are bread-and-butter work for these shops, and a motor swap is quick for them. Expect roughly £60-100 all in (motor plus labour), though prices vary. Ask for a quote first.
• Numatic's own repair service: Numatic, who make Henry, offer repairs. Check their website or call them for current options and pricing.
• Small appliance repair or PAT testing businesses often handle vacuums too.

When you drop it off, tell them what you've seen: rattly noise, weak suction, burning smell after about 5 minutes, and visible sparking through the top grille. That points them straight to the motor.

### Is it still worth it?
Yes. For well under half the price of a new Henry, you'll get a new motor with fresh bearings and brushes. That fixes the noise, the suction and the sparking in one go, and should give you plenty more years of use.
